result.headline: No roll-loop fault; yaw setpoint froze at 44 deg at t=83.3 s with no recorded cause
result.explanation: Roll and pitch follow their commands at a steady lag. The only freeze is the yaw setpoint, held at 44 from 83.3 s. Airspeed and yaw rate are constant 0, so those channels are dead or unrecorded. The recording does not show who commanded the yaw hold.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT control.attitude_setpoint[yaw] was varying, then held 44 from t=83.319 s to the end of the recording (6.237 s, 79 samples)
evidence.shows: Yaw command stopped varying and stayed at 44 deg until the end. Yaw attitude then settled near 48 deg (last 48.297), so the loop followed the frozen command. No mode change is recorded.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT vehicle.airspeed = 0 for the whole recording (1076 samples)
evidence.shows: Airspeed is 0 for the whole recording while ground velocity reaches about 20 m/s. The airspeed channel is dead or not populated. vehicle.yaw_rate is also constant 0 (line 29).

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.attitude[roll] changed level for good at t=7.508 s: median 41.539 before, 4.064 after deg (7.4x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The roll attitude shift follows a roll setpoint change that began at 7.367 s (cc_8). At best lag 0.959 s the correlation is 0.978 (cc_12), so this is a commanded manoeuvre, not a fault.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0 s controller.event[mavros: System] mavros: System: ERROR: Sensor helth
evidence.shows: A sensor-health error at t=0 fits the dead airspeed and yaw-rate channels. It appears at start-up only and is not tied to any later change.

checked.check: compare at 7.5 s and 25.4 s (roll shifts)
checked.result: The setpoint moved first, from 42.91 to -7.79 and from 42.91 to -15.52. Roll attitude followed with rising error only during the transition. No output froze.
checked.about: Roll control loop or actuator fault

checked.check: relation roll setpoint vs roll attitude, 5-30 s
checked.result: Correlation 0.845 rises to 0.978 at a 0.959 s lag. This is close to the steady 0.719 s lag removed by the tracking check, so there is no new lag.
checked.about: Roll control loop or actuator fault

checked.result: Yaw setpoint flagged frozen_after: true (spread 27.5 before, 0.0 after). The roll setpoint also stepped from 42.92 to -43.02. Roll tracking error rose 4.62x during the manoeuvre. Yaw tracking did not worsen (ratio 0.62).
checked.about: Yaw command source frozen or held

checked.result: The yaw setpoint dropped from 113 to 44 between 83.056 and 83.727 s and stayed at 44. Yaw attitude overshot to 92.9, then settled near 48. Actuators ch3-5 responded to the roll reversal at 84-86 s.
checked.about: Yaw command source frozen or held

checked.result: No earlier cases in the workspace.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a5 t=7.508 s: vehicle.attitude[roll] changed level for good (41.539 -> 4.064 deg) (see line 33; strength 2.033)
effects.why: Follows the roll setpoint change, so it is a response to the command.

effects.quote: ANOMALY a6 t=7.938 s: vehicle.attitude[roll] did not follow control.attitude_setpoint[roll] (peak |error| 16.389) (see line 77; strength 2.893)
effects.why: Transient error during a large setpoint step, with the steady lag already removed. It is not a persistent divergence.

data_requests.why_needed: Separates a commanded yaw hold from a stuck command, and a failed airspeed sensor from an unrecorded channel.

unobservable.fact: Pitot tube and airspeed sensor condition
unobservable.why_it_matters: A blocked or disconnected sensor would explain airspeed 0 and the sensor-health error.
unobservable.how_to_observe: Inspect the pitot and tubing, and read raw airspeed while blowing across the probe on the bench.

hypotheses.claim: The yaw setpoint froze at 44 deg at 83.3 s because of a stuck or ended command source.
hypotheses.because: It is the only output that stopped varying with no mode event. The yaw loop followed it, so the fault is upstream of the loop.

hypotheses.claim: The roll loop or its actuators failed to follow commands.
hypotheses.because: Roll follows its setpoint at a steady lag with correlation 0.978. Actuators ch3-5 respond to roll commands. This is observed in the estimate, not at the control surface.
hypotheses.observed_at: attitude estimate and actuator command outputs

hypotheses.claim: Airspeed and yaw-rate sensors are dead or unrecorded, matching the t=0 sensor-health error.
hypotheses.because: Both are constant 0 for the whole recording while ground speed is about 20 m/s. The data cannot say whether the sensors or the logging failed.

hypotheses.claim: Low battery voltage affected the controller.
hypotheses.because: The warning appears only at t=0. No later events, and no outputs froze or degraded as one would expect from a supply problem.

events.what: Low-voltage warning and sensor-health error at t=0
events.why: Start-up only. The sensor-health error is consistent with the dead airspeed channel.

events.what: Yaw setpoint held at 44 from 83.3 s to end
events.why: The only output that froze, with no recorded mode change or operator event.
Ground speed is about 20 m/s, so airspeed 0 is implausible.

events.what: Roll setpoint steps and the attitude following them
events.why: Commanded manoeuvres, tracked with a steady lag.

events.what: ch0, ch6 constant 1500 and ch7 constant 1926
events.why: Likely unused channels, with no relation to the control loops.
Marked as start-up and seen in healthy runs.

events.what: Throttle and actuator steps with setpoint changes
events.why: Throttle and the ch1/ch2 outputs move together, so these are controller responses.

result.lesson: No earlier cases are available; none applies.
